title: NY State Assembly · District 65
area: Lower Manhattan, including the Lower East Side, Chinatown, the Financial District, Battery Park City and part of the East Village.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Grace Lee is not seeking re-election. Illapa Sairitupac won a six-way June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 36.5% of the vote, defeating Jasmin Sanchez, Wei-Li Tjong, Jacky Wong, Mariama James and Lilah Mejia. Helen Qiu advanced from the Republican primary unopposed; she previously ran for this seat in 2022 (losing to Lee 76%-23.7%) and for New York City Council District 1 in 2025 (losing to Christopher Marte 71.6%-28%).

candidates.name: Illapa Sairitupac
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 36.5% of the vote.

summary.text: Illapa Sairitupac is a Lower Manhattan tenant organizer and social worker running as the Democratic nominee for this open seat, focused on housing affordability, taxing high earners, and opposing ICE enforcement in New York.

background.text: Son of Peruvian immigrants; has lived in the Lower East Side for almost 14 years.
Holds a Master of Social Work from NYU and previously worked as a mental healthcare worker.
Works as a tenant organizer and is an organizer with This Land is Ours Community Land Trust, which advocates for community land trusts in Lower Manhattan.
Was arrested in 2021 while protesting in support of the Build Public Renewables Act.

priorities.text: Taxing the wealthiest New Yorkers more, including a fairer progressive income tax and a state heirs tax, to fund housing, healthcare and childcare.
priorities.quote: I will fight for a fairer, more progressive income tax system and to implement a state heirs tax so that the very rich are contributing their fair share towards making New York affordable and equitable.

priorities.text: Housing as a human right: a state Social Housing Development Authority, rent-stabilization protections, and the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act.
Getting ICE 'out of New York,' including passing the New York for All Act to bar state and local government cooperation with ICE.
priorities.quote: We must protect our neighbors and get ICE out of New York.

positions.summary: Supports a more progressive state income tax and a new state heirs tax on large inheritances.
positions.quote: I will fight for a fairer, more progressive income tax system and to implement a state heirs tax so that the very rich are contributing their fair share towards making New York affordable and equitable.

positions.summary: Supports rent-stabilization protections and the Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act, and has organized tenant associations against displacement.
Opposes cooperation between state/local government and ICE and supports the New York for All Act; has led Know Your Rights trainings and anti-ICE organizing.
positions.quote: I'll fight to pass legislation like the New York for All Act, which bars state and local governments from colluding with ICE.

positions.summary: Supports universal healthcare and has advocated for the New York Health Act, which would guarantee coverage regardless of income or immigration status.
positions.quote: In Albany I'll continue to fight for the New York Health act, which would guarantee healthcare to all New Yorkers, regardless of income, immigration status or ability to pay.

positions.summary: Lists universal childcare among the causes he organizes for and would pursue in office.
Supports a faster transition to renewable energy, citing New York's low share of wind and solar power and his own organizing and arrest in support of the Build Public Renewables Act.

candidates.researchNotes: Sairitupac has not held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record. Positions are drawn from his 2026 and 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey responses, which are consistent with each other.

candidates.name: Helen Qiu
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed; third run for elected office (2022 Assembly, 2025 City Council).

summary.text: Helen Qiu is a former engineering project manager and pastor running as the Republican nominee for this open seat, focused on public safety, repealing cashless bail, and opposing what she calls government overreach.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Zhongshan University (1990), a graduate degree from Reformed Theological Seminary (2007), and a graduate degree from Columbia University (2010).
Career experience includes working as a pastor, teacher, engineer and engineering manager.
Affiliated with the New York City Education Council.
Ran for this Assembly seat in 2022, losing to Grace Lee 76%-23.7%, and for New York City Council District 1 in 2025, losing to Christopher Marte 71.6%-28%.

priorities.text: Public safety: repeal cashless bail reform, fund the NYPD, and improve prison conditions.
Housing: preserve NYCHA from sale and prioritize affordable housing for seniors and single-parent families.
Education: uphold merit-based admissions and defend the SHSAT and Gifted & Talented programs.
Small businesses: reduce regulations and taxes and protect small landlords' property rights.

positions.summary: Supports repealing cashless bail and increasing funding for the NYPD.
positions.quote: Repeal Cashless Bail reform, improve prison conditions, fund NYPD

positions.summary: Opposes congestion pricing, listing it among taxes she would stop.
Frames her housing position around defending small landlords' property rights rather than expanding tenant protections.
positions.quote: Defend small landlords as small businesses, protect private property

candidates.researchNotes: Qiu has not held elected office and did not complete a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey for 2026, 2025, 2024 or 2023; her most recent documented statement of positions is her 2022 survey response (still linked from her current, active Ballotpedia candidate page), so priorities/positions here may not reflect any 2026-specific updates. No current campaign website was found; only social-media profiles, which were not accessible to this agent.

researchNotes: Neither candidate has held elected office, so neither has an official voting/bill record. Sairitupac's positions come from his own 2026 Ballotpedia survey; Qiu's most recent available candidate statement is her 2022 survey (she has not completed the Candidate Connection survey since).
